title: My daughter asked for cute bees, so I made a cozy bee game with Claude Code (open source, no asset files)
author: zernonia
selftext:
Hey r/aigamedev! I just launched **Hivebound**, a cozy 3D exploration game in the browser: you're a tiny bee on a hex island. You gather nectar, befriend wild bees, build up a hive for the Queen, and eventually fly past the mist into new lands.

▶ Play (free, no account): [https://hivebound.zernonia.workers.dev](https://hivebound.zernonia.workers.dev)   
📦 Source (MIT): [https://github.com/zernonia/hivebound](https://github.com/zernonia/hivebound)

# Why bees?

A few of the mechanics were inspired by **Palworld**: gathering resources, building up your base, befriending (well, "capturing") creatures out in the world, and assigning them tasks. I wanted to see how those ideas would feel in something much gentler. Here you do a little dance to befriend wild bees, then give them jobs: gathering nectar or pollen, or helping out at the honey press, bee bread kitchen and wax works.

And the bees are this cute because of my **wife and daughter**. They asked for "cute bees", and that became the design brief: big shiny eyes, rosy cheeks, little wiggly antennae, and keepsakes to dress your bee up in (a sunflower clip, a lily-pad hat, a royal ribbon…). Several design decisions came from watching them play.

# How it was made

I built it with **Claude Code (Opus 5.5)** in about 3 days, \~14k lines across 63 files. My role was mostly game director and playtester. I wrote the feature requests, played every build and pushed back on the feel. Claude wrote the code, tested it and opened the PRs.

**Stack:** Nuxt 4 + TresJS (three.js for Vue) + Pinia, deployed as static files on Cloudflare Workers.  
(Why Nuxt? Because I'm a Vue developer 😂)

# Things that worked really well

* **Zero asset files.** Every model is built in code: the bee, trees, the hive, the cottage and all the wearable keepsakes. Props are merged vertex-coloured geometry drawn as instanced meshes. The **music is synthesised live** with Web Audio, a generative piece that gets warmer inside the hive and hushed at night, with crickets. No licensing headaches, and the whole game is tiny.
* **A preview link on every PR.** Each branch gets a Cloudflare preview, so I tested every change before merging (and my family tested them too 😄). A short [CLAUDE.md](http://CLAUDE.md) told Claude to always post the link.
* **Claude tested its own work in a headless browser.** It ran the game in Chromium, set up save states through the stores, screenshotted scenes and checked things like "does this dialog show once and never again after reload?".
* **A scripted balance bot.** To tune the economy, Claude wrote a "sensible player" bot that plays chapter one on a virtual clock using the real game stores. It caught a soft-lock (a full store blocked your pouch forever) and told us the chapter takes \~13 bot-minutes, or \~40 human minutes.
* **Deterministic world generation.** When chapter two added a new ring of land, the old island was generated in exactly the same order, so existing saves kept every tile (verified: 0 of 1,801 tiles changed).

# Where I had to steer

* **Feel is a human job.** "The native `<select>` looks out of place", "the build menu causes layout shift", "don't auto-fly me into the hive": small taste calls like these made the biggest difference, and the AI didn't catch them on its own.
* **Balance needed real numbers.** A sealed hive cell cost 3 wax, and it only felt right at 1. The bot helped, but playing it myself was what settled it.
* **Visual bugs slip past text.** A roof rendered invisible because the geometry's point order was reversed. It only came up because we looked at screenshots.



Happy to answer anything about the workflow, prompts, or the procedural art. It's a cozy game give it a try!

comments.body: A very cute game. Admittedly, I didn't realize right away that I needed to stand on the little island while the nectar collected - the pink filling-up circle is barely visible. It might be worth making it a bit more distinct.

comments.body:
https://preview.redd.it/ax8tm52gfnsh1.png?width=721&format=png&auto=webp&s=6db3b5661657a16655f512824013a9980ec31c39

Speedrun?

replies.author: zernonia
replies.body: Brooooo you're the first to complete (as far as I know)! How was it? Speedrun sounds like a fun idea tho, how long you took to complete it?

replies.author: JezzabelOfficial
replies.body: I showed it to my partner as she loves these kinds of games. Did a run through where I had \~20 bees, then the queen asked me to befriend a lavender bee. But I was already at the 20 bee cap, even after building more bee rooms. So restarted, and completed it in... 20 mins? such a cozy game <3

replies.author: zernonia
replies.body:
Yeah I capped it at 20 bees to make sure wide range of browser support (cpu consumption), probably need to add a feature to 'let go' bees. 

20 mins sounds perfect! What do you think a speedrun leaderboard? I imagine there'll be more ways to optimize the workflow and completion time 😉

replies.author: JezzabelOfficial
replies.body: Expect some PRs coming your way

replies.author: JezzabelOfficial
replies.body: There you go mate, added the ability to dismiss bees, and change the max bee limit. Now I can have an Army 😄

replies.author: zernonia
replies.body: Awesome! Thanks for the PR! 💛

comments.author: nberthdev
comments.body:
This looks and feels very good to play. Two quick pieces of criticism:

Personally I could've used more onboarding, wasn't sure what I was doing and what I was meant to do, and I probably could've figured it out but instead I dropped out. 

Also in some cases there's a bit too little breathing space on the screen, like in the hive, on my little phone screen all of the screen real estate feels very busy.

Amazing none the less. How expensive was this to produce?

replies.author: zernonia
replies.body:
Thanks for your kind word and the feedbacks!

Onboarding was purposely excluded, as a mean for player to discover the game by itself (inspired by palworld, where I had to learn those mechanic without guide 😂), I understand that some player requires it to not feel 'lost' in it. Will see how I can improve it! 

Yeah playing on smaller is a challenge to solve, I've tried to optimise abit but sometimes it can be cluttered and unable to navigate properly. Will slowly improve this!

comments.author: Either-Complex11
comments.body: Let the record show that I like bees

comments.author: barret232hxc
comments.body:
love it. And I love how you included the areas that a real human is needed. I think a lot of people miss that while you can prompt a game in oneshot as people have shown, to make something like this it needs a game designer/director to make the vision shine.

I bet your daughter thinks you're the coolest Dad around, I've been making cutesy styled games with flowers and my daughter loves it

replies.author: zernonia
replies.body:
Thanks for your kind word! Really appreciate it! I dont wanna just share some vibe-coded stuff, I want to create my vision in mind.

My daughter just looveeeee the cute little bees!!! 🐝🐝🐝

replies.author: barret232hxc
replies.body: yeah, I think there are a lot of assumptions when AI is used, or when people hear vibe coded. I see you put in effort to this. We need more posts like this, and the fact you made it open source to help others learn, or expand on the game is really cool.

comments.author: orellanaed
comments.body: The preview link on every PR is the part I'd steal, having your family play each branch before it merges is a real playtest loop and most AI built games skip it. Building every model in code with vertex colours is probably why the bee and the trees read as one game.

comments.author: barret232hxc
comments.body: So I decided to play it, and now I can't stop, I didn't realize how much stuff there was to do. My main feedback is always about game juice and game feel, I think you could add a cool effect when you drain a resource from a tile, I think that would just feel really satisfying and give the player some quick feedback they got all the resources, just like a cool effect on the tile maybe with some particles or a glow, but either way I'm really enjoying the game

replies.author: zernonia
replies.body:
Really glad that you are enjoying it! 🐝

Currently draining the tile does have a small visual cue (fading), a cool effect sounds awesome too!

replies.author: barret232hxc
replies.body: also, my daughter was watching me play on my laptop and she's like asking me if can play, but she's almost 5 so she only really knows how to use phones so I put it on the phone and she just loved moving the bee around even though she didn't really know how to properly play, she was having a blast. So just know your game brought joy to my daughter as well.  It immediately caught her attention so you really got something going on here

replies.author: zernonia
replies.body: Bro that is really awesome to hear! You've made my day 💛🐝
